extracted.intended_audience: scientists invited to act as PCI Plants recommenders / associate-editor-like editorial role for preprints
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recommenders who manage peer review of preprints for PCI Plants: responsibilities include selecting reviewers, collecting reviews, making editorial decisions, and (if positive) writing a 300–1500 word recommendation. Emphasis on methodological/ethical soundness and Open Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint eligibility: scientific quality, methodology, ethics, Open Science
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI only accepts ('recommends') preprints of high scientific quality that are methodologically and ethically sound and that adopt Open Science practices, such as open data and open code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI wishes to promote reproducibility and reliability; recommend only articles that meet these standards. Importance or impact of results should not be a criterion for acceptance. There is no required acceptance/rejection rate; accept all articles that meet the high scientific, methodological and ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research question/hypothesis clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The research question/hypothesis/prediction must be clearly presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear, request revision; if not corrected, reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear justification of sample sizes must be provided for empirical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification should address, as relevant: statistical power, Bayes factor thresholds, or estimate precision (quantitative studies) and information power or saturation thresholds (qualitative studies). Refer to Lakens (2022) for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions supported by results; no overstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The results must adequately support the conclusions, and the analysis's interpretation must not be overstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conclusions are not supported or are overstated ask for revision or reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data availability and metadata quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data must be available and reusable, except where ethical restrictions apply (e.g., risks to humans, animals or the environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata and accompanying text must accurately describe the data. If data cannot be shared for ethics reasons, this should be clearly stated and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis and simulation code availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Details concerning quantitative analyses (data treatment and statistical scripts) and simulations (scripts, codes) must be available to the reader in the text or through a correctly versioned deposit in an open repository with a DOI or other permanent identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repositories like Zenodo, Dryad or institutional repositories. Git URLs are not permanent; provide a DOI or other permanent ID (e.g., Software Heritage SWHID). Scripts/code must be carefully described so another researcher can reuse them. The page links to guidance on assigning DOIs for GitHub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedure detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Details on experimental procedures must be given in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure enough methodological detail for reproducibility; request revisions if procedures are insufficiently described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approvals where required
rubrics_metrics.description: In fields requiring approval from an ethics committee or IRB, authors must ensure the proposed research has received all necessary approvals before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify declarations of approvals and ethical compliance; request documentation or reject if missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and signatory role
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders are responsible for editorial decisions and will sign all decisions sent to authors. If co-recommenders are present, responsibility is shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Managing Board validates or requests modification of decisions. Do not delegate decision-making solely to reviewers; make independent editorial judgments and cite the information used to reach the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness: invitation response and handling deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply rapidly to invitations to handle an article by accepting or declining, and commit to ensuring the evaluation process is conducted in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no recommender decides to handle a submitted article within usually 20 days, the article is automatically desk-rejected. Send invitations to multiple potential reviewers within 48 hours of agreeing to handle a manuscript. Reviewers are typically expected to write reviews within 3 weeks, and you are expected to make your decision within 10 days after reviews are completed or after receiving a revised version. Post your editorial decision or recommendation text within 10 days of receiving the reviews or revised manuscript. Inform the Managing Board if delays are likely or if you cannot carry out duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who to accept an invitation: willingness, interest, expertise, time, no COI
rubrics_metrics.description: You must handle a manuscript evaluation only if you are willing, find the preprint interesting, have enough relevant expertise, have time to handle it through the whole process, and have no actual/potential/perceived conflict of interest as specified in the PCI Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these are not met, decline the invitation. Major flaws discovered early may justify desk rejection, but you should have read the article carefully before agreeing to handle it; desk rejections after handling should remain extremely rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest avoidance in reviewer invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite reviewers without conflict of interest with the authors or with the content of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search broadly and avoid reviewers who have actual, potential or perceived conflicts. Follow the PCI Code of Conduct definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer numbers and recruitment strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Find at least two reviewers willing to review the preprint; send invitations to multiple potential reviewers (often 5–10 initially) because not all will accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start inviting reviewers as soon as you agree to handle the manuscript or receive a revised version. The process of finding reviewers should ideally take no more than one week. If reviews received are too light, search for additional reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: When inviting reviewers consider a broad mix of scientists with different scientific perspectives, institutional affiliations, career stages, and personal characteristics (e.g., geographic origin, ethnicity, gender).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity is encouraged to capture multiple perspectives and improve review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalise invitation letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Try personalising your invitation letters as much as possible to maximise response rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalisation increases acceptance likelihood; tailor invites to expertise and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make decisions based on at least two good-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an editorial decision based on at least two good-quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack sufficient quality in reviews, seek more reviewers. Do not let reviewers alone make the decision; synthesize reviews with your own assessment and cite all information used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and adherence to Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Be kind, respectful, and constructive in your decisions; adhere to the PCI Code of Conduct and avoid abusive or discriminatory language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions violating the code may be returned for editing or discarded. Maintain professionalism in communications with authors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use impact/importance or negative results to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance or impact of the results should not be a criterion for acceptance. Do not use negative results as grounds for rejecting an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate on methodological/ethical/scientific soundness rather than perceived novelty or positive findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and presentation checks
rubrics_metrics.description: If the language is poor, mention it to the authors and suggest they check for typographical errors and/or have the text reviewed by a language professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to typographical and grammatical errors when requesting revisions; you do not need to check reference formatting (optional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision content: summarise reviews, add own criticisms, state disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your editorial decision should summarise the most relevant comments of the reviews and your own points of criticism, and state whether you disagree with some points raised by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not copy-and-paste reviewers' comments into your decision (reviews are automatically attached). Cite all information and comments used to reach your decision in addition to peer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to reject at any stage for scientific reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Feel free to reject an article at any step of the evaluation process if scientifically sound reasons justify this rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections after several rounds are permissible when justified. If you reject, reviews and decision will be sent to authors but will not be published; they are stored securely and accessible to the Managing Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform Managing Board about delays, inability, or suspected misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the Managing Board if there is likely to be any delay, if you are unexpectedly unable to carry out recommender duties, or if you suspect scientific misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely communication helps the Managing Board intervene (e.g., reassigning). Suspected misconduct should be reported for appropriate handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage policy for decisions and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: You must absolutely not use AI to generate your decisions or recommendation texts. Using AI for generation risks rejection of your text by the Managing Board and being banned from PCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use AI only to translate, correct and improve texts (e.g., language polishing), but not to produce substantive decision content or the recommendation text itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation text: format, length and content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you decide to recommend the preprint, you must write a recommendation text: a short article (similar to a News & Views piece) with its own title, containing 300–1500 words, describing the context and explaining why you find it interesting and why you decided to recommend it. The text must contain references (at minimum the recommended article).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use AI to generate the recommendation text. Read past recommendations in your PCI for examples. Use the provided question prompts to structure the recommendation (context, your interest, methodological strengths/robustness, notable aspects, concise main results, reviewer improvements, points reviewers appreciated, points you appreciated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and citation of recommendations and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When PCI publishes your recommendation, it signifies that PCI considers the article scientifically valuable; recommendations and associated articles can be cited in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommended, PCI publishes the evaluation correspondence (peer reviews, editorial decisions, and authors' answers) with reviewers retaining the right to choose anonymity or signing. Authors remain free to publish recommended articles in traditional journals; PCJ offers an open-access publication option with no fees or further peer review. Several PCI-friendly journals may use PCI evaluation to replace, accelerate or complement their procedures.
